title: Nuggets face Jazz in 2026-27 preseason opener
seoTitle: Nuggets face Jazz in 2026-27 preseason opener
subtitle: Denver's first game with its new lineup draws attention to three players seeking the spotlight
excerpt: The 2026-27 preseason opener between the Denver Nuggets and Utah Jazz highlights Christian Braun, Alpha Diallo, and DaRon Holmes, who could define the.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The opening game of the 2026-27 preseason between the Denver Nuggets and Utah Jazz has arrived on the schedule, sparking interest among fans who want to see how Denver's new lineup performs after offseason adjustments.

Christian Braun seeks redemption after inconsistent season

Power forward Christian Braun takes the court with expectations of improving his performance after a campaign marked by injuries and inconsistency. Last season, his offensive output and perimeter defensive presence were questioned, raising doubts about the $125 million contract signed before the season. The game against the Jazz will be the first opportunity to assess whether Braun will return with explosiveness and efficiency, both in his outside shooting and drives to the basket.

Alpha Diallo makes NBA debut after EuroLeague stint

Alpha Diallo, 29, arrives in Denver after winning the EuroLeague Best Defender award, playing in Greece and Monaco. Standing 2.01 m tall, weighing 91 kg, and with a 2.08 m wingspan, he has the physical tools to make his presence felt on perimeter defense. His first official NBA game will be against the Jazz, and the amount of minutes he receives, as well as his defensive role, will be closely analyzed.

DaRon Holmes tries to expand role after injury

DaRon Holmes, who overcame an Achilles tendon injury in 2024, enters the game with the possibility of receiving more playing time. The absence of Spencer Jones, who is still treating a thigh injury, could open up space for Holmes to play more in the fourth. His performance as a scorer and versatile defender will be crucial, especially after Peyton Watson's departure to the Cleveland Cavaliers, which left the team in search of young talent.

Expectations for the Nuggets vs. Jazz matchup

The matchup, scheduled for Sunday at 5:00 PM (Denver time) at the CU Events Center, will be broadcast locally and on NBA TV. Although it is a preseason game, the presence of promising young players and the possibility of rotating minutes among veterans create an intense evaluation scenario for both clubs. The Jazz, who recently moved up to second place in the draft and selected Darryn Peterson, will also look to test their new pieces.

What fans should watch for

In addition to the individual performances of Braun, Diallo, and Holmes, the audience should keep an eye on the style of play that the Denver team's head coach intends to implement, as well as how the young players adapt to the rhythm of the NBA. The outcome of the game may not define the season, but it will offer valuable indicators of the team's competitiveness in the Western Conference.

With information from Sports Illustrated, SLC Dunk.
